{"notes":"2026-11-25: the store half is DONE, the wire half is blocked.

DONE, and committed:

* Store::fanout_window(room) -> (oldest still held, highest assigned).
  The oldest is read from the surviving room_event rows, not from a
  stored cutoff, so it follows retention exactly (§6: mimid offers
  catch-up over message_retention_secs, and the two cannot drift). The
  highest comes from room.next_fanout_seq, so it still names a fanout
  whose events have been pruned -- which is what makes §5.1's DISTINCT
  out-of-window answer possible instead of a short one.
  Test: the_fanout_window_follows_retention_and_the_counter.
* Store::serves(room, domain, seq), the §8 entitlement bound, with five
  tests (bead mimid-1wgh.37.104.2).

BLOCKED on bead mimid-1wgh.37.104.6: where a catch-up answer carries
its sequences. Decision mimid-1wgh.104 put the sequence beside the
message, which bead mimid-1wgh.37.104.1 implemented as a header -- fine
for /notify, which carries exactly one fanout, but a catch-up answer
carries many (§5: "fanouts in hub order, each with its sequence") and
one header cannot pair them. That is wire format for the protocol-08
text of decision mimid-1wgh.105, so it is Mark's call.

AND THE DIRECTORY TEMPLATE IS DELIBERATELY NOT PUBLISHED. §5 makes
publishing it the whole of the capability negotiation -- "a provider
that does not publish the template does not support it" -- so it must
appear in directory.rs only when the operation works, in the same
commit. It goes in Directory::unknown, not as a new typed field: the
field is not in protocol-07 §5.1 and `unknown` exists to round-trip
exactly this, so no protocol-07 wire type changes."}

{"notes":"2026-11-25, second pass. The WIRE FORMAT is now in; the HANDLER is
blocked again, on a different question.

DONE, beyond the store half recorded above:

* mimi-protocol::catchup, the bodies, as decision mimid-1wgh.37.104.6
  settled them: CatchUpRequest { from, limit } and CatchUpResponse
  { highest_sequence, entries<V> } with each CatchUpEntry carrying its
  own sequence beside its FanoutMessage. Presentation language written
  out in the rustdoc, limits as named constants marked INVENTED
  (CATCH_UP_LIMIT 256, MAX_CATCH_UP_ENTRIES).
* crates/mimi-protocol/tests/catchup.rs, 10 tests. Every fixture byte is
  hand-encoded from that presentation language or taken from the
  vendored mlswg vectors; none comes from the encoder under test. The
  RFC 9420 §2.1.2 length-prefix helper is checked against prefixes read
  off tests/update_notify.rs, since it is my code and not the crate's.

WHAT THE DECODER REFUSES, each one a choice about where a disagreement
surfaces: a limit of 0; entries not strictly increasing (a follower
applies them in order and hub order is room order, so sorting would
hide which end is wrong); sequence 0 (a fanout from before the sequence
existed cannot be named); an entry above highest_sequence (the highest
is the counter, so it cannot be below what was just served); trailing
bytes and every truncation.

DELIBERATELY NOT AN ERROR: a gap in the returned sequences. Retention
(§6) and the §8 window both bound what a hub serves, so a skipped
sequence is expected, and §5.1's distinct refusal is what says a request
cannot be filled. In the module's # Limitations so it is not read as an
oversight.

A limit above the cap is served SHORTER, not refused, because §5 already
lets a hub return fewer.

STILL BLOCKED, now on bead mimid-1wgh.37.104.7: the hub does not store
the FanoutMessages a catch-up answer is made of. room_event.bytes is the
MLSMessage; the fanout body is in the outbox until delivery;
follower_event has them but only for rooms this provider follows, and a
room hubbed here with only remote members never delivers to it.

ALSO STILL TO DO when that lands: the route, the §5.1 refusal as a
distinct status and RFC 9457 problem type (410 Gone with its own type
reads right: the range existed and is gone), and the catchUp directory
template, which must appear only in the same commit as a working
operation because publishing it IS the capability negotiation (§5)."}

{"notes":"DONE 2026-11-25. The handler, the route, the two refusals and the
directory template.

* hub/catchup.rs serves the operation; Hub::catch_up is the entry.
* POST /v1/catchUp/{roomId} in http.rs, authenticated by the From
  header as every other peer endpoint is.
* HubError::CatchUpOutOfWindow -> 410 Gone, problem type
  catch-up-out-of-window. Gone says the range existed and does not any
  more, which is the follower's situation and tells it to surface a gap
  rather than retry.
* HubError::CatchUpNotEntitled -> 403, catch-up-not-entitled.
* HubError::CatchUpCorrupt for a stored fanout that will not decode:
  this hub's own corruption, so a 500 rather than a refusal.
* The catchUp template is published in Directory::unknown, which exists
  to round-trip a key protocol-07 §5.1 does not define, so no
  protocol-07 wire type changes. It lands in THIS commit because
  publishing it is the whole of the capability negotiation (§5).

THREE DECISIONS THE DESIGN NOTE DID NOT FORCE:

1. §5.1 IS CHECKED BEFORE §8. A requester whose own fanouts are all
   pruned would otherwise be told it was never entitled, which is
   false; it is told its request is too old, which is true and
   actionable.
2. §5.1 IS JUDGED AGAINST THE ROOM'S OLDEST SURVIVING FANOUT, not the
   requester's. This is the cost of dropping the participation ranges,
   made concrete: the rows that would say whether THIS requester was
   entitled to a pruned sequence die with their events. So a request
   reaching before the room's oldest is refused even when the requester
   was never a destination of that part. It errs towards refusing,
   which is the safe direction, since the failure §5.1 exists to
   prevent is a short answer that looks whole. Written into the
   module's rustdoc under "What this hub cannot tell".
3. highest_sequence is the REQUESTER's highest, not the room's. For a
   provider still in the room they are the same, because every fanout
   reaches it; for one that has left, the room's would say the
   conversation continued without it, which §8 says it should not learn.

TESTS, crates/mimid-server/tests/hub_catchup.rs, six:

* an_in_window_request_returns_the_range_after_what_the_follower_holds
* the_limit_is_honoured_and_the_answer_says_there_is_more
* an_out_of_window_request_is_refused_and_not_served_short -- drives the
  REAL retention sweep (Store::delete_expired_events), not a hand
  DELETE, so it holds §6's coupling as well: catch-up reaches exactly
  as far back as the hub log, and the sweep is what moves it.
* a_provider_that_was_never_a_destination_is_refused
* an_unknown_room_or_a_bad_body_is_an_error
* a_served_fanout_is_byte_identical_to_what_was_delivered -- the
  assertion the handler's decode-and-re-encode rests on. I had twice
  argued the round trip is the identity because mimid decodes
  canonically; that is reasoning, and this is evidence.

STILL NOT DONE, and each its own bead: the follower does not ASK
(mimid-1wgh.37.104.4), and no two-provider test recovers a real gap
(mimid-1wgh.37.104.5). So the hub answers catch-up and nothing yet
calls it."}
